subject: Math
title: Trigonometry, transformations & vectors
sub: Pythagoras and trigonometry, sine and cosine rules, 3D and trig graphs, transformations and vectors
strategyIntro: Extended Maths is two papers of equal weight: Paper 2 (2 hours, 100 marks, no calculator) and Paper 4 (2 hours, 100 marks, calculator). Your school test may be shorter, but it is marked the same way: M marks for a correct method, A marks for the correct answer that follows, B marks for a correct result on its own.

strategy.title: Timing
points: About 1.2 minutes per mark: a 5-mark question is worth about 6 minutes.
If a question has taken twice its time, leave a gap and come back at the end.
Keep 10 minutes at the end to check answers against the question.

strategy.title: Show your working
points: Most marks are method marks. A wrong answer with clear working can still score most of the marks.
Write the calculation you are doing before the answer, e.g. 360 ÷ 12 = 30.
An answer with no working can score zero if it is wrong, and sometimes even if it is right ("show that").

strategy.title: Paper 2: no calculator
points: Practise fractions, negative numbers, standard form and surds by hand.
Leave answers exact when you can: fractions, surds, or in terms of π.
Check with a quick estimate: is the answer about the right size?

strategy.title: Paper 4: calculator
points: Give answers to 3 significant figures unless the question says otherwise; angles to 1 decimal place.
Never round partway through. Keep the full value in the calculator memory (or write 4+ figures).
Use the π button, not 3.14. Check the calculator is in degrees.

strategy.title: Answer the question
points: Read the last line again: units, form of answer ("in its simplest form", "in terms of π"), and accuracy.
"Show that" questions: every step must be written, ending with the given result.
When the question says "hence", use the previous part.

commandWords: Calculate
Work out from given facts. Show the working; usually a calculator is allowed.
Work out / Find
Get the answer by any correct method. Show working.
Write down
The answer needs little or no working: you can often read or state it.
Show that
The answer is given. Write every step clearly so the examiner can follow the logic to it.
Estimate
Round each number (usually to 1 significant figure) and calculate a rough value.
Simplify
Write in its simplest form: collect like terms, cancel common factors.
Factorise (completely)
Write as a product of factors. Completely means take out every common factor.
Expand
Multiply out the brackets.
Solve
Find the value(s) of the unknown that make the equation or inequality true.
Sketch
Show the shape and key features (intercepts, turning points), not plotted accurately.
Describe fully
For a transformation: name it and give every detail (centre, angle, direction, scale factor, vector or mirror line).
Hence
Use the result you have just found to answer this part.
Give your answer in its simplest form
Cancel fractions and ratios fully; simplify surds.
quizIntro: Quick calculations and concept checks. Do each one on paper first, then pick. The wrong options are common mistakes, so if you got one, read the working in the explanation.
flashIntro: Methods, rules and formulas. Say the rule out loud (or write it down) with an example before you tap, then check you remembered every step.

flashcards.back: a² + b² = c², where c is the hypotenuse (the longest side, opposite the right angle).

flashcards.front: Finding a shorter side with Pythagoras
flashcards.back: Subtract: a² = c² − b². Check your answer is shorter than the hypotenuse.
sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse; cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse; tan θ = opposite/adjacent.
Use the inverse function: θ = sin⁻¹(opp/hyp), cos⁻¹(adj/hyp) or tan⁻¹(opp/adj).
Both are measured from the horizontal: elevation looking up, depression looking down. They are equal (alternate angles).
Measured clockwise from north, written with three figures (e.g. 045°). The back bearing differs by 180°.
Make sure the calculator is in degrees (D on screen), not radians.
a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C. Use it when you know a side and its opposite angle.
sin A/a = sin B/b. Put the unknown angle on top.
a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A. Use with two sides and the angle between them.
cos A = (b² + c² − a²) ÷ 2bc. Use when all three sides are known.
½ab sin C, where C is the angle between sides a and b.
Label each side with the letter of the opposite angle. If you know a side and its opposite angle, use the sine rule; otherwise use the cosine rule.

flashcards.front: Obtuse angles and the sine rule
flashcards.back: sin θ = sin(180° − θ). When the sine rule gives an angle, the obtuse angle 180° − θ may also be possible (the ambiguous case).
cos of an obtuse angle is negative. If the cosine rule gives cos A < 0, angle A is obtuse.
d = √(a² + b² + c²) for edges a, b and c.

flashcards.front: Angle between a line and a plane
flashcards.back: Drop a perpendicular from the end of the line to the plane. The angle is between the line and its projection (shadow) on the plane.
Find the right-angled triangle that contains the length or angle you need. Draw it separately in 2D, label it, then use Pythagoras or SOHCAHTOA.
A wave with period 360°. Starts at (0, 0), maximum 1 at 90°, back to 0 at 180°, minimum −1 at 270°.
Period 360°. Starts at (0, 1), 0 at 90°, minimum −1 at 180°, 0 at 270°, back to 1 at 360°.
Period 180°. Through (0, 0) and (180°, 0). Asymptotes (it is undefined) at 90° and 270°.

flashcards.front: Solving sin x = k for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°
flashcards.back: x₁ = sin⁻¹ k, x₂ = 180° − x₁. If x₁ is negative, add 360° to it.

flashcards.front: Solving cos x = k for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°
flashcards.back: x₁ = cos⁻¹ k, x₂ = 360° − x₁.

flashcards.front: Solving tan x = k for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°
flashcards.back: x₁ = tan⁻¹ k, x₂ = x₁ + 180°.
"Reflection in the line …" with its equation, e.g. y = x, x = 2, y = −1.
"Rotation, [angle] [clockwise/anticlockwise], centre (a, b)." A 180° rotation needs no direction.
"Translation by the vector (x over y)". Top number: right (+) or left (−). Bottom number: up (+) or down (−).
"Enlargement, scale factor k, centre (a, b)." Find the centre by drawing lines through corresponding points; they meet at the centre.
Between 0 and 1: the image is smaller and closer to the centre.
The image is on the opposite side of the centre and upside down (as if also rotated 180°).
Give exactly one transformation with all its details. Two transformations score nothing.
In y = x: (a, b) → (b, a). In y = −x: (a, b) → (−b, −a). In the x-axis: (a, b) → (a, −b). In the y-axis: (a, b) → (−a, b).
Anticlockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). Clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). In the exam use tracing paper.
x is the movement right (+) or left (−); y is up (+) or down (−). Written as bold a, or AB with an arrow.
Add the components. In a diagram, follow one vector and then the other (nose to tail).
|(x, y)| = √(x² + y²), the length of the vector.
AB = OB − OA = b − a.
To find a vector, go along a route of known vectors. Travelling a vector backwards changes its sign: BA = −AB.
One is a scalar multiple of the other: 3a − 6b = 3(a − 2b), so it is parallel to a − 2b and 3 times as long.
Show AB = k × BC (so they are parallel) AND say they share the point B.
If P divides AB in the ratio 1 : 3, then AP = ¼ AB.
If M is the midpoint of AB, OM = ½(a + b).

quiz.q: A right-angled triangle has shorter sides 7 cm and 24 cm. How long is the hypotenuse?
In a right-angled triangle, tan θ = 5/12. What is sin θ?
quiz.why: Opposite 5, adjacent 12, so hypotenuse 13 (5, 12, 13). sin θ = opp/hyp = 5/13.

quiz.q: A 6 m ladder leans against a wall, making 70° with the ground. How high up the wall does it reach?
quiz.why: Height is opposite the 70° angle, ladder is the hypotenuse: 6 sin 70° = 5.64 m. 6 cos 70° = 2.05 m is the distance from the wall.

quiz.q: The bearing of B from A is 125°. What is the bearing of A from B?
What is the exact value of cos 30°?
From 50 m away on level ground, the top of a 20 m tower is seen. What is the angle of elevation?
quiz.why: tan θ = 20/50 = 0.4, θ = tan⁻¹ 0.4 = 21.8°. Using sin⁻¹ 0.4 gives 23.6°.

quiz.q: You know b = 7, c = 9 and A = 50°. Which rule finds side a?
quiz.why: Two sides and the included angle: cosine rule. There is no right angle, so Pythagoras and SOHCAHTOA don't apply.

quiz.q: A triangle has sides 8 cm and 10 cm with 30° between them. What is its area?
Which is equal to sin 150°?
quiz.why: sin 150° = sin(180° − 150°) = sin 30° = 0.5. Sine is positive for angles between 0° and 180°.

quiz.q: A triangle has sides 5 cm, 7 cm and 8 cm. What is the angle opposite the 7 cm side?
In triangle ABC, a = 12 cm, A = 40° and B = 65°. Find b.
quiz.why: b/sin 65° = 12/sin 40°, so b = 12 sin 65° ÷ sin 40° = 16.9 cm. Swapping the sines gives 8.51 cm.

quiz.q: A cuboid measures 3 cm by 4 cm by 12 cm. How long is its space diagonal?
Solve sin x = 0.5 for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°.
Solve cos x = −0.5 for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°.
What is the period of y = tan x?
Solve tan x = 2 for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°.
Reflect the point (3, −2) in the line y = x.
quiz.why: Reflecting in y = x swaps the coordinates: (−2, 3).

quiz.q: Which column vector translates (1, 4) to (−2, 9)? (Written as (x, y).)
An enlargement with scale factor −2 and centre (0, 0) maps (1, 3) to:
quiz.why: Multiply each coordinate by −2: (−2, −6). The image is on the other side of the centre.

quiz.q: Rotate (4, 1) through 90° anticlockwise about the origin.
quiz.why: (x, y) → (−y, x): (−1, 4). (1, −4) is the clockwise rotation.

quiz.q: Which is a complete description of a rotation?
quiz.why: A rotation needs angle, direction and centre.

quiz.q: A shape is enlarged by scale factor 3. How many times bigger is its area?
What is the magnitude of the vector (−5, 12)?
OA = a and OB = b. Which is the vector AB?
quiz.why: A to B: go back along a, then along b: −a + b = b − a.

quiz.q: Which vector is parallel to 2a − 3b?
quiz.why: −4a + 6b = −2(2a − 3b), a scalar multiple, so it is parallel (opposite direction).

quiz.q: OA = a, OB = b and M is the midpoint of AB. Find OM.
quiz.why: OM = a + ½(b − a) = ½a + ½b = ½(a + b).

examIntro: Paper 2 / Paper 4 style. [No calculator] questions are Paper 2; [Calculator] questions are Paper 4. Write full working first, then open the mark scheme: M1 = method mark, A1 = accuracy mark (correct answer from correct working), B1 = mark for a correct result on its own. Give yourself one mark per point you got.

exam.q: [Calculator] A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse 13.5 cm and one other side 8.2 cm. Find the length of the third side.
[Calculator] A ship sails 15 km due north from P to Q, then 8 km due east from Q to R. Find (a) the distance PR (b) the bearing of R from P.

[Calculator] From the top of a cliff 85 m high, the angles of depression of two boats, which are in a straight line with the foot of the cliff on the same side, are 32° and 21°. Find the distance between the boats.
points: M1: angle of elevation from each boat equals the angle of depression (alternate angles)

exam.q: [Calculator] In triangle PQR, PQ = 9 cm, PR = 11 cm and angle QPR = 48°. Find the area of the triangle.
[Calculator] In triangle PQR, PQ = 9 cm, PR = 11 cm and angle QPR = 48°. Find the length of QR.
[Calculator] Town B is 40 km from town A on a bearing of 070°. Town C is 25 km from B on a bearing of 190°. (a) Show that angle ABC = 60°. (b) Find the distance AC. (c) Find the bearing of C from A.
points: B1: bearing of A from B is 250°, so angle ABC = 250° − 190° = 60°
exam.note: Draw a sketch with north lines at A and B first.

exam.q: [No calculator] Sketch the graph of y = cos x for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360° and write down the coordinates of its minimum point.
points: B1: correct shape from (0, 1) through (90, 0), (270, 0) to (360, 1)

exam.q: [Calculator] ABCDEFGH is a cuboid with base ABCD. AB = 8 cm, BC = 6 cm and the vertical edge CG = 5 cm. Find (a) the length of the diagonal AG (b) the angle between AG and the base ABCD.
[No calculator] Triangle A has vertices (1, 1), (3, 1) and (1, 2). It is translated by the vector (−4 over 3). Write down the vertices of the image.
[No calculator] Triangle P has vertices (2, 1), (4, 1) and (4, 2). Triangle Q has vertices (−1, 2), (−1, 4) and (−2, 4). Describe fully the single transformation that maps P onto Q.

[No calculator] Triangle T has vertices (2, 2), (4, 2) and (2, 6). (a) Find the vertices of the image of T after an enlargement, scale factor −½, centre (0, 0). (b) Find the vertices of the image of T after reflection in the line y = x. (c) Describe fully the single transformation that maps the image from part (a) back onto T.
[No calculator] p = (2, −3) and q = (−1, 4). Find 3p + 2q as a column vector.
[No calculator] A is the point (2, 5) and the vector AB = (6, −8). Find (a) the coordinates of B (b) |AB|.

[No calculator] OA = a and OB = b. P is on AB so that AP : PB = 1 : 2. C is the point with OC = 2a + b. (a) Find AB in terms of a and b. (b) Find OP in its simplest form. (c) Show that O, P and C lie on a straight line.
points: M1: OP = OA + AP = a + ⅓(b − a)
A1: so OC = 3 OP: OP and OC are parallel
A1: and they share the point O, so O, P and C are collinear
